literal: that which has come down; tradition, scripture

definitions.definition: Revealed Śaiva scripture spoken by Śiva/Sadāśiva, the 'higher knowledge' as against the lower knowledge beginning with the Veda; in South Indian usage especially the 28 Siddhānta scriptures and their upāgamas.
The Pāñcarātra saṃhitās as scripture spoken by Bhagavān himself (Bhagavacchāstra).

notes: A widely quoted etymology (ā-gata from Śiva's mouth, gata to Girijā, mata by Vāsudeva) is of uncertain source and not recorded as a definition here.

definitions.definition: A revealed scripture, so called because it expands (tanoti) matters of the principles and mantras and protects (trāyate).

The initiatory division of Śaivism whose scriptures (Siddhānta and non-Saiddhāntika tantras) give both powers/enjoyment and liberation through initiation, mantra-worship and yoga; the fifth and highest stream after the worldly, Vedic, spiritual and Atimārga paths.
In the Mantramārga's own scriptures, the ascetic Śaiva path (Pāśupata and Lākula) ranked above Vedic and 'spiritual' religion but below the Mantramārga.

notes: U17 owns lin:atimarga and its own account; this is the Mantramārga's classification.

definitions.definition: A stream of Śaiva revelation issuing from one of Sadāśiva's five faces: Siddhānta (upper), Gāruḍa (east), Vāma (north), Bhūta (west) and Bhairava (south); the Kāmika also counts twenty-five by the five faces each being fivefold.
The five-faced form of Śiva (faces Īśāna, Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, Vāmadeva, Sadyojāta) from whom all tantras issue; the 28 Siddhānta tantras are the limbs of his mantra-body.
Sadāśiva's five faces, identified with the five brahma-mantras (Īśāna, Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, Vāmadeva, Sadyojāta), whose combinations yield the Śiva-, Rudra- and Bhairava-tantras.

literal: division (of scripture) belonging to the Śivas

definitions.definition: The first ten of the 28 Siddhānta tantras (Kāmika to Suprabheda), revealed to ten Śivas; in Jayaratha's reading they are dominated by difference (bheda).

literal: division (of scripture) belonging to the Rudras

definitions.definition: The eighteen Siddhānta tantras from Vijaya to Vātula, revealed to eighteen Rudras; in Jayaratha's reading dominated by difference-and-non-difference.
Any of the 28 root Siddhānta scriptures, as distinct from their sub-divisions (upāgama/upabheda); installation rites should be done with a mūlāgama.

A subsidiary scripture attached to one of the 28 mūlāgamas; the Kāmika calls them upabheda ('sub-divisions') and lists 206 by the counts it gives (the usual traditional total is 207); the Kiraṇa says a division within the divisions is an upabheda.
The account of how the one knowledge was divided and taught by Śiva to Śivas and Rudras and handed down through chains of divine, semi-divine and human recipients.
One of the four sections of an ideal Āgama: knowledge (vidyā/jñāna), ritual (kriyā), yoga, and conduct (caryā); all of Śiva's scriptures are said to have the four pādas.
The Pādma Saṃhitā is arranged in the same four pādas (jñāna, yoga, kriyā, caryā).
The division of the Bhairava tantras centred on a male Bhairava, chiefly Svacchandabhairava.
The division of the Bhairava tantras centred on goddesses and feminine mantras (vidyā), comprising Yāmala and Śakti tantras.
A class of Vidyāpīṭha tantras named for the union of Bhairava and the goddess (e.g. Brahmayāmala, Jayadrathayāmala); the Śrīkaṇṭhīya's second group of eight.
The scriptures of the upper stream — the 28 Śiva- and Rudra-tantras and their upāgamas.
Each of the four Pāñcarātra divisions (Mantra-, Āgama-, Tantra-, Tantrāntara-siddhānta), so called because those settled in Mīmāṃsā and other śāstras become eligible for it.
Scriptures of the eastern stream for neutralising poison with Garuḍa mantras.
Scriptures of the western stream (Sadyojāta) for controlling and expelling spirits.
Scriptures of the left/northern stream centred on Tumburu and his four sisters (e.g. Vīṇāśikha).
A ritual manual systematising the procedures of the Āgamas (e.g. Somaśambhu's, Aghoraśiva's).
The Īśānaśivagurudevapaddhati as a principal authority of Kerala temple ritual.
A revealed Pāñcarātra text; tradition speaks of 108 (the Jayākhya's additional passage), of which the Sātvata, Pauṣkara and Jayākhya are the 'three gems'.
The Sātvata, Pauṣkara and Jayākhya saṃhitās, held to issue directly from the Lord's mouth; the Īśvara, Pārameśvara and Pādma are their explanatory expansions.

notes: Not the Buddhist or Jain 'three jewels' (different ids).

definitions.definition: The scripture and tradition of Bhagavān; the Pādma derives the name from the five other śāstras becoming 'night' before it; other explanations link it to Nārāyaṇa's five-day rite (ŚB 13.6.1).
Name of the Veda-branch claimed as the root of the Pāñcarātra; Vedānta Deśika's Pāñcarātrarakṣā gives primary eligibility to the Ekāyanins.

notes: The Chāndogya (7.1.2) lists an 'ekāyana' among Nārada's studies; the identification is the tradition's.

definitions.definition: A follower of the Pāñcarātra; opponents held the Bhāgavatas/Sātvatas to be a low temple-serving class, Yāmuna that they are brahmins so named for a quality.
Name for the Pāñcarātra's followers and teaching (the 'Sātvata teaching'); in Manu 10.23 a Sātvata appears among the offspring of degraded twice-born, which opponents used against the Bhāgavatas.

The rite performed on the soul — not on caste or body — by which the guru, empowered by Śiva's mantras, joins the soul to Śiva and destroys its bonds; it is the cause of the other means (ritual, knowledge, conduct).
Initiation into Bhagavān's mantras and worship, in Śrīvaiṣṇava usage centred on the five sacraments (pañcasaṃskāra).
The first Śaiva initiation, making one a samayin, entitled to worship and study under the post-initiatory observances (samaya).
In several Siddhānta sources a name for the initiation (often identified with or following samaya-dīkṣā) that qualifies for personal Śiva-worship.
The liberating initiation that purifies the six paths (adhvan) and burns past and future karma, leaving only the karma that sustains the present body, which is exhausted by experience.

Initiation in which the post-initiatory observances are purified away for those unable to keep them (children, the foolish, women, the old, the sick), their liberation coming through devotion; contrasted with sabīja ('with seed') initiation for the capable.

notes: The Kiraṇa passage teaches the practice without using the word.

definitions.definition: Initiation after which the initiate must keep the observances (samaya), for those capable of them.
Consecration conferring the office of teacher (ācāryābhiṣeka) or of power-seeker (sādhakābhiṣeka).
Bathing of the installed image; in Kerala, kalaśa-abhiṣeka rites renew the deity's power.
The post-initiatory rules binding the initiate; for those unable to keep them they may be purified away, and knowingly breaking them is a great fault.
The lowest grade of Śaiva initiate, after samaya-dīkṣā.
An initiate who has received nirvāṇa-dīkṣā and seeks liberation.
An initiate consecrated to master a mantra for supernatural powers and enjoyments (bubhukṣu).
The consecrated teacher (also deśika, guru) empowered to initiate and to perform installations.

literal: one wishing to enjoy / one wishing to be liberated

definitions.definition: The two orientations of Mantramārga initiates: seeking powers and enjoyments in the higher worlds, or seeking liberation; the Mantramārga caters for both.
The twofold fruit that all four pādas of Śiva's scripture serve.
Figurative name for Śiva's awakening of the soul by his power, like a teacher waking sleeping pupils; it occurs when the soul's karmas are in equilibrium, and its sign is a distinctive devotion.
Name used by 'those who hold to the āgamas' for Viṣṇu's compassion, his fifth power of grace, by whose glance the soul's karmas become equal and it is lifted from saṃsāra.

equivalents.note: The Ahirbudhnya identifies kṛpā, anugraha-śakti and śaktipāta; the Śaiva texts also treat śaktipāta as the working of grace.

definitions.definition: The state in which opposed karmas are equal, neither exceeding the other, marking the time of śaktipāta.
The equality of karmas that the soul attains when looked upon by Viṣṇu with grace; the two karmas fall silent.
The Lord's fifth power/act — grace — called compassion (kṛpā) and śaktipāta; one of Lakṣmī's five acts.
The first of Lakṣmī's five acts, the concealing power by which souls are bound.
The soul: eternal, formless, ignorant, inactive, without qualities or lordship, pervasive, lodged in māyā and bound through kalā, vidyā, rāga, prakṛti and the instruments.

notes: Contribution from U08; U18 owns the Siddhānta definition.

definitions.definition: Worship of Śiva with mantras, twofold: for oneself (in the liṅga received at initiation) and for others (in temples, for king and realm), preceded by the five purifications.
Ijyā, worship of Bhagavān, the third of the five daily periods.
Arcana of Viṣṇu in a consecrated image with Vedic mantras; the best of the means.
The daily sequence of temple pūjās performed by the śānti under the tantri's authority.
Private worship by an initiate in the liṅga given by the guru or on a ground-altar, for one's own fruit.
Public temple worship on behalf of king and realm, performed by qualified priests in installed liṅgas.
Purification of oneself, the place, the substances, the mantras and the liṅga before worship.
The ritual-meditative dissolution of the body's elements into their sources and the re-creation of a pure, divine body before worship (the Kāmika's 'self-purification' corresponds in function).
Purification of the elements performed before worship of Bhagavān.
Performed by the tantri in the preliminary sequence of Kerala worship.
Placing mantras (e.g. the five brahma-mantras and six limbs) on the body and on the image to make them divine.
Placing mantras on the body (and, in another sense, 'depositing' oneself — see trm:nyasa-surrender).
Placing of mātṛkā and deity mantras, as taught in the Prapañcasāra and Śāradātilaka.
Surrender of oneself to the Lord, which alone attains what other means cannot; equated with the six-limbed śaraṇāgati.

equivalents.note: AS 37 treats nyāsa and śaraṇāgati as one

definitions.definition: Six-limbed refuge: resolve to do what pleases, avoidance of what displeases, faith that he will protect, choosing him as protector, laying down oneself, and helplessness.

equivalents.note: Śrīvaiṣṇava usage treats prapatti, śaraṇāgati and nyāsa as one

definitions.definition: Mental worship of the deity in the heart and body before external worship.
Mental worship (mānasayāga) preceding external worship.
External worship of the deity in liṅga, image, maṇḍala or fire.
Offerings into the consecrated fire in a kuṇḍa, part of daily and occasional worship.
The formless (amūrta) worship of Viṣṇu through fire offerings.
The prescribed fire-pit, of various shapes, for homa; described in the Kāmika's kuṇḍa chapter.
The coloured diagram on which the deity is worshipped, especially at initiation.
Diagram for worship and initiation, richly described in the Pauṣkara.
A levelled ground-altar used as a support of worship, e.g. for one's own worship.
The aniconic form of Śiva used in worship; the Kāmika distinguishes self-manifest, divine, bāṇa, sages' and man-installed liṅgas, and the liṅga given by the guru at initiation.
Installation and consecration of liṅga, image or temple, to be performed with a single root āgama.
Consecration of images and temples (e.g. the Hayaśīrṣa's subject).
Installation of the fixed and movable images.
Installation of the seven deities, performed only by the tantri.
The first of the temple-building rites (ploughing the site), opening the series that ends in installation.
Rites for renovating a temple or replacing a damaged image.
Renovation followed by re-consecration (punaḥpratiṣṭhā) under the tantri.
The annual temple festival (mahotsava) with flag-hoisting and processions.
The annual festival conducted by the tantri.
Rites that make good lapses in ritual and observance.
Annual offering of a thread-garland (pavitra) to Śiva in Śrāvaṇa or Nabhasya, removing all defects in the year's worship.
Annual pavitra offering to Viṣṇu with the same function.
Śiva's powers present as sound-forms through which ritual acts; the perfected mantras paralyse and destroy the soul's bonds in initiation.

notes: Contribution from U08; U31 owns mantra theory.

definitions.definition: Hand gestures shown to the deity and in purificatory acts during worship.
The six 'paths' of the cosmos — letters, words, mantras, kalās, principles and worlds — purified in nirvāṇa-dīkṣā.
The five cosmic divisions — nivṛtti, pratiṣṭhā, vidyā, śānti, śāntyatīta — into which the principles are grouped and which are purified in initiation.

notes: Not to be confused with trm:pancakala (Pāñcarātra five periods).

definitions.definition: The hereditary Nampūtiri brahmin ritual authority of a Kerala temple, who alone performs installation, festivals and major purifications.
Resident priests who perform the daily pūjās in a Kerala temple under the tantri's authority.
Procession of the deity's image around the shrine with offerings to the attendant deities, performed at fixed times of the temple day.

literal: offering to the Lord's attendant beings

definitions.definition: Offering of cooked rice to the deity's attendants (bhūtas and guardians) placed around the shrine.
A consecrated water-pot in which the deity is invoked for bathing and installation rites.
Kalaśa rites (e.g. sahasrakalaśa) by which the tantri renews an installed deity's power.
The eight-ingredient binding compound that fixes the image to its pedestal, periodically renewed with rites.
Used likewise in Tamil temple practice (aṣṭabandhana).
The Vidyāpīṭha sādhaka's observance in Kāpālika style (cremation ground, skull) while mastering a goddess-mantra; recorded in summary only.

literal: the Blessed One, possessor of bhaga

definitions.definition: The Lord as possessor of the six qualities (ṣāḍguṇya).
Knowledge, power, lordship, strength, virility and splendour, together constituting the supreme Brahman; knowledge is its very form, the other five its aspects; they are also Lakṣmī's body.

notes: Not the three guṇas of prakṛti; the AS calls Brahman 'nirguṇa' with respect to those.

definitions.definition: The Lord's will-power (saṅkalpa) — his resolve 'may I be many' — personified as his discus; the Ahirbudhnya's central principle, of which even the Sāṃkhya is said to consist.
Nārāyaṇa's eternal, independent power, whose body is the six qualities and who performs his five acts.
The four emanated forms of the Lord — Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha — each manifesting a pair of the six qualities while possessing all six.
The supreme Lord and first vyūha, full of all six qualities.
The vyūha manifesting knowledge and strength; in Śaṅkara's report of the Bhāgavatas, identified with the individual soul.
The vyūha manifesting lordship and virility; in Śaṅkara's report, identified with mind (manas).
The vyūha manifesting power and splendour; in Śaṅkara's report, identified with ego-sense (ahaṃkāra).
The fifth of the five forms of Viṣṇu invoked in Vaikhānasa worship.
The Lord's descents; the Ahirbudhnya counts thirty-nine, beginning with Padmanābha.
The supreme form of Bhagavān (Para Vāsudeva) in his highest realm, first of the five modes.
The Lord dwelling within beings, one of his five modes.
The Lord present in a consecrated image, the most accessible of his five modes.
The image of Viṣṇu in which he is worshipped; image worship is the best means.

The creation proceeding directly from the six qualities — the vyūhas and their realm — as distinct from the 'other-than-pure' creation from prakṛti; the Jayākhya places the Vaiṣṇava creation before the prādhānika and brāhma creations.
The five periods of the Pāñcarātrin's day: abhigamana, upādāna, ijyā, svādhyāya, yoga.
The first daily period: purification and approaching the Lord (going to the temple).
The second daily period: gathering flowers and other materials for worship.
The third daily period: worship of Bhagavān.
The fourth daily period: study of scripture and recitation.

notes: Contribution from U08 (Pāñcarātra sense); Yoga's niyama sense is U10's.

definitions.definition: The Vaiṣṇava initiation in Pāñcarātra-based Śrīvaiṣṇava usage: branding (tāpa) with discus and conch, the sectarian mark (puṇḍra), a new name (nāma), the mantra, and worship (yāga).
Branding of the upper arms with the discus and conch, first of the five sacraments.
Not undergone by Vaikhānasas, who hold that they are Vaiṣṇavas from the womb.
A brahmin following the Sūtra of Vikhanas; the Vaikhānasa Sūtra is held to be the first and best of sūtras and 'Vikhanas' to denote Nārāyaṇa.

notes: In Dharmaśāstra the word also names a class of forest hermits.

definitions.definition: The Vaikhānasa self-description: made Vaiṣṇavas before birth by the prenatal viṣṇubali rite, they need no further Vaiṣṇava initiation such as branding.
Prenatal saṃskāra in the eighth month of pregnancy dedicating the child to Viṣṇu.
Viṣṇu's partless highest form (represented by the fixed image, receiving only flowers) and his partite, gross form (represented by the movable image, receiving full worship).
Śiva as partless (niṣkala), partite (sakala) and both (sakala-niṣkala, e.g. the liṅga).
The supreme Lord as sakala, from whom Śakti, Nāda and Bindu arise.
The immovable principal image standing for Viṣṇu's partless form.
The smaller movable image, linked to the fixed image, standing for Viṣṇu's partite form and receiving the full daily worship.
The principal fixed image in the sanctum.
The principal installed liṅga or image.
The five images of a Vaikhānasa temple: fixed (dhruva), movable worship (kautuka), festival (utsava), bathing (snapana) and offering (bali) images.
Viṣṇu, Puruṣa, Satya, Acyuta and Aniruddha, the five forms invoked in Vaikhānasa worship.

equivalents.note: both are sets of divine forms for worship; the Vaikhānasas do not present theirs as vyūhas

definitions.definition: Worship of Viṣṇu in a consecrated image, as distinct from formless (amūrta) worship through the fire.
Worship of Viṣṇu through fire offerings, without an image.
Hereditary Vaikhānasa priest serving a Viṣṇu temple.
Temple priest (in Tamil Śaiva usage the Ādiśaiva/Śivācārya).
In Lakṣmīdhara, the Vedic way of Goddess worship taught in the five 'auspicious āgamas', opposed to the Kaula and 'mixed' ways.

notes: Contribution from U08; U23 owns Śrī Vidyā doctrine.

definitions.definition: The Vasiṣṭha, Sanaka, Śuka, Sanandana and Sanatkumāra saṃhitās, which in Lakṣmīdhara's account teach the Vedic Samaya way.
The sixty-four Bhairava tantras in eight groups of eight (Śrīkaṇṭhīya).
The sixty-four tantras 'of the Mothers' named in the Vāmakeśvara, by which Paśupati 'beguiled the world' before revealing the Goddess's own tantra (Saundaryalaharī 31).
The resonance arising from Śakti in the unfolding from the supreme Lord, from which Bindu arises.

notes: Contribution from U08; U31 owns nāda.

definitions.definition: The point arising from Nāda in the Śāradātilaka's account of emanation.

notes: Contribution from U08; U31/U28 own bindu.
